To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the incremental joint approach to POS tagging & parsing in Chinese is the first of its kind, and that the approach achieves the state-of-the-art on both the POS tagging and parsing tasks.

the incremental joint approach is superior to the baseline and the pipeline approach in both POS tagging (F-score of 95.5% vs 93.8% and 94.2%) and dependency parsing (F-score of F1 87.2% vs 83.7% and 86.0%), and the incremental joint approach achieves the new state-ofthe-art performance in Chinese POS tagging and dependency joint task.

1) the joint approach to POS tagging & dependency parsing is more effective than the traditional pipeline approach; 2) the incremental approach is more effective than non-incremental approaches; and 3) delayed features are effective to overcome the difficulties of the incremental joint approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) How to jointly perform POS tagging and dependency analysis in Chinese? (2) How to incrementally perform joint POS tagging and parsing? (3) How to address the problem of underspecified POS tags in the incremental setting?

the following contributions: 1) we propose an incremental approach to joint POS tagging and parsing in Chinese; 2) we propose the delayed feature mechanism to deal with the underspecified POS tags; 3) we achieve the new state-ofthe-art performance in joint POS tagging and syntactic parsing.
the following questions: 1) Can joint POS tagging and parsing achieve better performance than the pipeline approach?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the joint approach outperformed the baseline and pipeline systems by 1.2 and 0.7 points on the POS tagging task respectively, and by 1.4 and 2.2 points on the dependency parsing task respectively.
the proposed joint model is superior to the pipeline approach in the joint task.

our approach achieved substantial improvements in both POS tagging (F-score 96.6%) and dependency parsing (F-score 90.4%), which outperform the previous best reported results (F-score 95.8% and 87.8%) on the Penn Chinese Treebank.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an efficient and accurate joint approach to POS tagging with dependency parsing.

the incremental approach to joint POS tagging and parsing can effectively reduce the error propagation problem and improve the performance of joint POS tagging, and the dynamic programming framework can be extended to deal with the problem of underspecified tags.
the proposed approach is a simple and effective way of joint POS tagging, dependency parsing, and even other related tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the joint approach is a better choice to achieve the best performance in both POS tagging as well as dependency parsing.
joint POS tagging and parsing can benefit each other in Chinese.
the incremental approach can be applied to joint tasks of POS tagging and dependency syntax parsing in Chinese.
